Wound tables

Designer-reviewed working entries consolidated from the design discussion in issue #1125. These replace the compact placeholder table. They have not been balance simulated. Numerical fixtures and their comparative balance remain subject to tests.

Procedure and notation

Use the wound roll in @UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.player-rules.JournalEntry.3a45aacf3898e8b3.JournalEntryPage.9303127ab1b28c3b]{recovery}: retain the highest three dice, sort lowest to highest, and read the result. There are 56 possible entries per table: 21 in the 100 band, 15 in 200, 10 in 300, 6 in 400, 3 in 500, and only 666 in 600.

Select the damage type that dealt the most damage after resistance; the player chooses on a tie. Physical includes sonic and force. Fire, Cold, and Lightning use Elemental; Mental, Radiant, and Life/Necrotic each have their own table. This shared Elemental table does not merge the individual elemental resistances.

If every damage component is reduced to zero and the minimum 1 total damage causes a wound, the player chooses among the attack's original damage types.

Example: an attack deals 2 Physical and 1 Fire damage, both fully resisted. Its minimum 1 damage drops the character to 0 HP. The player chooses the Physical or Elemental wound table.

If the body part is absent or the injury does not apply, move down to the next valid listed result until an applicable entry is reached (for example 116 → 122). Every table ends in 666, Last Words. Players choose source-appropriate descriptions with the DA; existing choices of comparable injury remain subject to applicability.

Immediate consequences happen once: push, pull, and knockdown are not recurring wound effects. Use existing forced movement, terrain, and collision rules. The DA chooses a direction consistent with the injury. A push followed by Prone can be described as a throw; no separate airborne throw mechanic is introduced here.

Temporary conditions use @UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.player-rules.JournalEntry.341fafd96c17a900.JournalEntryPage.b8dbac21301a8aa3]{conditions}: resolve end-of-turn effects, then decrease by 1. No entry uses a separate short-duration Dazed or Paralyzed rule. An asterisk prevents automatic decay. Blinded and Deafened have one effect; their numbers measure duration, not severity. Lasting movement penalties and Banes remain until their printed remedy, rather than decaying as if they were conditions. The DA decides when a Bane to physical or mental activities applies.

Treatment: one attempt per wound per day, even with several healers. Weak / Standard / Strong adds 1/2/3 cumulative progress. Meet or exceed the Recovery Value (RV) to remove the listed lasting effect. Progress remains with the wound. A dash means no treatment track, not an automatic healing roll. Temporary conditions end by decay or their normal remedies; treatment does not itself extinguish or staunch them. One treatment track resolves the listed treatable effects of one wound.

Example: Physical 333 applies Bleeding 1 and a lasting Bane. Bleeding can decay or be reduced by an appropriate Main Action; it does not recur because the wound remains. Soft Tissue treatment reaching RV 3 removes the Bane. The scar still counts.

All wounds leave scars that permanently count toward future wound rolls. Cosmetic wounds need no treatment. Where treatment softens a socially significant scar, it removes both the intimidation Boon and persuasion Bane, not just the drawback. Rest alternatives must be printed explicitly; there is no universal rest timer.

Severity and required treatment cards

BandGuidelineRV for treatable effects
100Mostly cosmetic/social; occasional minor condition or −1 movement near upper end1–2; none for cosmetic-only entries
200Individual conditions, 1 Bane, or −1/−2 movement2–3
300Combinations; stronger conditions3–5
400Severe conditions, 2 Banes, or movement penalties up to −35–7
500Devastating combinations, movement penalties up to −4, or permanent losses7–9 when treatable
666Last WordsNo ordinary treatment

Treatment capabilities supplied by the current card catalog: Soft Tissue Treatment, Bone Treatment, Elemental Wound Treatment, Mental Wound Treatment, Radiant Wound Treatment, Life Wound Treatment. These are broad capabilities, not a separate ability for each injury. The treatment cards print their attributes, discipline requirements, costs and time. Treatment is limited to one attempt per wound per day, with 1/2/3 progress by outcome.

Treatment cannot regrow a lost body part. An artificial limb or explicitly restorative ability specifies what it remedies. Scars remain even after functional recovery. Physical wounds leave minor scars in 100–200, moderate scars in 300–400, and major scars in 500. Mental scars do not dictate personality, allegiance, or choices. Elemental scars are visibly more pronounced, including at low severity.

Open test concerns: wounds usually occur while Dying, so immediate Dazed or Paralyzed may matter most after prompt healing. Burning/Freezing are resistible; Bleeding is not. Frightened depends on a perceptible source. These differences need testing, not an assumption that equal ratings create equal danger.

Elemental

Every entry leaves a permanent visible scar, even when its only effect is temporary. Burning/Freezing means Burning for Fire or Lightning and Freezing for Cold. Burning still deals Fire damage; Freezing deals Cold damage. The wound source does not change a condition's damage type. Elemental 556 converts the earlier single-turn Paralysis to Paralyzed 1 under the shared decay rule.

BandOrdinary clothing consequence

300Clothing covering the injured area is ruined

Every result leaves a mental scar even after temporary effects clear. The player chooses its expression; no personality, allegiance, or behavior is imposed. Frightened uses the creature or phenomenon responsible as its source and now decays normally; it no longer has the earlier until-safely-away duration. Later reminders do not automatically reapply it. Mental sensory wounds need not injure eyes or ears.
